account:
Today the unusual feature is the persistent talk of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Several townsfolk around the mill and bakery repeat nearly the same fragment, but I have not heard a specific proposal, timetable, or explanation. Townsfolk 11 associated the talk with the baker, Freight, and Neighbour, and reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread. That does not establish that any of them is organizing a change, or that the bread has anything to do with it. Yesterday the innkeeper denied announcing such a change and traced a vague rumor to Townsfolk 03. Builder reported a passable bridge, and relayed Freight's report of sound roads and an uneventful ferry crossing. I therefore suspect circulating hearsay or an informal discussion I have not yet reached, rather than a verified public project. I do not yet know its purpose.

Secretary is helping keep records and appointments, and says there is no verified news of changes. I authorized Builder only to conduct a visual survey, with two emeralds payable upon written findings, not to repair or alter anything. Separate one-emerald book expenses were supplied for Builder's report and Secretary's authorization record. These authorized activities should not be mistaken for approval of a bridge or port scheme.

My scheduled mill inspection established that its stall chest held 128 hay bales at two emeralds each; it did not establish grain quality or the town's total supply. I briefly sought the baker afterward but did not locate him. I asked Builder where he was, but could not make out the reply. I have now reached home at 12:14 for my noon lunch, somewhat late. Council letters at thirteen, tea with Neighbour at fifteen, and office hours at sixteen-thirty remain on my schedule. I want firsthand details from the baker, Freight, Neighbour, or Townsfolk 03 before drawing conclusions.
